* Legend

- IP: the initial page, before any button. FRP: the final rendered page (our table).
- States: yes: Works; part: Works for some of the page's links only; no: No preview; na: Does not apply (no such page part).
- Evidence: spec: A fixture spec asserts it; `spec` names the file and a test-title substring; code: Read from the code; no spec asserts it; inferred: Believed from the code's shape, not traced to the end.
- 2b cells: H opens in the window (Back returns), T new tab, T! new tab and a gap, - no such window there.
  A plain left click; Ctrl, Shift, Alt, ⌘ or the middle button always keep the new tab.

** Notes

- n1: On its own site a detail link opens in the site's own window; it needs that site's preview switch (Brucebase shows also sa_bb_event_preview).
- n2: Read by the generic reader: the window shows a plain web page, not Brucebase's parsed show.
- n3: setlist, artist and venue pages need sa_pop_ext_setlistfm_key; without it only /search?artist= is read, and on setlist.fm itself the others keep their new tab.
- n4: On discogs.com a Discogs page no reader takes is the site's own link and keeps its new tab.
- n5: Only once the record has loaded (see G8).

** Windows

- MusicBrainz entity: mb-entity on musicbrainz.org; dg-mb on discogs.com and setlist.fm
- Discogs (6 readers): discogs, dguser, dgsearch, dgsupport, dghistory, dgimages: onAreaClick → _extDgDrill()
- Wikipedia: allLinksReaders
- Wikidata: allLinksReaders
- setlist.fm: allLinksReaders
- Springsteen detail: the springsteen reader, or the site's own window on its own host
- Brucebase show (year#date): the bbdate reader; also the MB-Event glyph's window
- archive.org item: the iadetails reader
- YouTube: the youtube reader
- Other web page: the generic reader

* Gaps

** G1 Brucebase gig, venue and relation links leave the window

Evidence: code. Code: _extDpTest().

Away from discogs.com and Brucebase itself, a Brucebase /gig:, /venue: or /relation: link in a Springsteen, Brucebase show, archive.org, YouTube or web-page window opens a new tab; in the other windows it opens as a plain web page. _extDpTest() adds the site's ownLinks on discogs.com only, so elsewhere these links are the generic reader's.

** G2 MusicBrainz links leave the window on the Springsteen sites and archive.org

Evidence: code. Code: _MB_FOREIGN_POP_HOST, _dgMbWinTarget().

On springsteenlyrics.com, jungleland.it, brucespringsteen.it, brucebase.wikidot.com and archive.org, a musicbrainz.org link in any window opens a new tab: the MB entity source is off on a foreign host, and _MB_FOREIGN_POP_HOST covers discogs.com and setlist.fm only.

** G3 A Brucebase show link on Brucebase leaves the window

Evidence: code. Code: _extTarget(), _DP_SITES['brucebase.wikidot.com'].

On brucebase.wikidot.com, a /<yyyy>#<ddmmyy> link in a window opens a new tab: it is the page's own host (_extTarget() returns null), and /<yyyy> is neither a detail URL nor one of the site's ownLinks.

** G4 No previews on the initial page of dg-search, ia-search and the sfm-* pages

Evidence: code. Code: _DP_SITES[…].extRoot.

dg-search's content is in <main>, which _DP_SITES['www.discogs.com'].extRoot does not name. archive.org's links are in shadow DOM, and setlist.fm's extRoot names only our own section (#mb-sfm-root), not the site's div.body.

** G5 The MB importer's icons on Discogs' older layout get no card before a render

Evidence: code. Code: _dgMbSource().

On the #page_content pages (submissions, history, images, user, ratings, sell), the dg-mb source's selector names #app only, so murdos' MusicBrainz icons in Discogs' own content have no card on the initial page. Not checked: whether the importer puts icons on those pages at all.

** G6 "All credits on Discogs ↗" opens the same artist again in the window

Evidence: code. Code: _extDgArtistHtml() (the mb-dg-box), _extDgDrill().

The link is /artist/<id>?type=Credits. The discogs reader has no keyUrl, so its key differs from the artist window's own, and _extDgDrill() opens the same artist in place instead of the website's credits in a new tab.

** G7 Wikipedia's "A table: show it on Wikipedia ↗" can reopen the same article

Evidence: code. Code: _extWpLeadFor().

The link is rebuilt from the API's resolved title with encodeURIComponent. When the window was opened from a redirect or from a URL spelled differently (a literal comma, as MusicBrainz stores them), the key differs and the click opens the same article in the window instead of Wikipedia in a new tab.

** G8 A Discogs window opens nothing in place until its record has loaded

Evidence: code. Code: _extDiscogsAreaClick().

Before the record arrives, a click on a link in a Discogs window keeps its new tab, while the hover marks (_dpWinWhat()) already say it opens here.
